========================================================
  BSHH Attack S4 — Malicious Controller, With RSU      
========================================================

  t=5.000   ①  V0 <-> V1: Normal V2V heartbeat exchange
  t=5.000   ②  V0/V1 -> RSU: DSRC heartbeat forwarding
  t=5.010   ③  RSU -> Controller: legitimate aggregate (CSMA)
  t=5.100   ④  Malicious Controller stores stale copies from RSU aggregate
  t=10.000  ⑤  Controller internally replays stale HBs (no external packet)
  t=10.000  ⑥  Controller holds conflicting liveness -> faulty routing

  LOG FORMAT: controllers printed as Ctrl<idx>(ns3=<id>), RSUs as RSU<idx>(ns3=<id>), vehicles as V<idx>(ns3=<id>)
  Every selected malicious controller executes STEP ④, ⑤, ⑥.

========================================
  PAIR: ATTACKER=Ctrl0(ns3=0)  VICTIMS=V5(ns3=10)/V45(ns3=50)  RSU=RSU0(ns3=205)
========================================
[t=5.000]  STEP ①  NORMAL V2V HEARTBEAT EXCHANGE
  V5(ns3=10) -> V45(ns3=50) : Heartbeat(Sender=V5(ns3=10), beacon_sending_time=5.000)
  V45(ns3=50) -> V5(ns3=10) : Heartbeat(Sender=V45(ns3=50), beacon_sending_time=5.000)

[t=5.000]  STEP ②  VEHICLES FORWARD HBs TO RSU (DSRC broadcast)
  V5(ns3=10) --[DSRC broadcast]--> RSU0(ns3=205) : Heartbeat(Sender=V5(ns3=10), beacon_sending_time=5.000)
  V45(ns3=50) --[DSRC broadcast]--> RSU0(ns3=205) : Heartbeat(Sender=V45(ns3=50), beacon_sending_time=5.000)

[t=5.010]  STEP ③  RSU FORWARDS LEGITIMATE AGGREGATE TO CONTROLLER (CSMA)
  RSU0(ns3=205) --CSMA--> Ctrl0(ns3=0) : Heartbeat(Sender=V5(ns3=10), beacon_sending_time=5.000)  ACCEPTED
  RSU0(ns3=205) --CSMA--> Ctrl0(ns3=0) : Heartbeat(Sender=V45(ns3=50), beacon_sending_time=5.000)  ACCEPTED

[t=5.100]  STEP ④  MALICIOUS CONTROLLER STORES STALE COPIES (from RSU path)
  Attacker Controller : Ctrl0(ns3=0)
  captured_packet for V5(ns3=10) : Heartbeat(Sender=V5(ns3=10), beacon_sending_time=5.000)  (from STEP ③ RSU aggregate)
  captured_packet for V45(ns3=50) : Heartbeat(Sender=V45(ns3=50), beacon_sending_time=5.000)  (from STEP ③ RSU aggregate)
  Action : Ctrl0(ns3=0) stores both stale copies for internal replay (STEP ⑤)

[t=7.000]  STEP ⑤  CONTROLLER INTERNAL REPLAY (RSU path variant, no external packet)
  Attacker Controller : Ctrl0(ns3=0)
  Packet source       : stored STEP ④ stale copies (captured from RSU aggregate)
  Overwrites V5(ns3=10) liveness with V5(ns3=10)'s own stale beacon_sending_time=5.000 (correctly attributed, just old)
  Overwrites V45(ns3=50) liveness SLOT with a FORGED heartbeat
    physical_sender (true slot owner) = V45(ns3=50)
    claimed_sender  (forged identity)  = V5(ns3=10)
    Ctrl0(ns3=0) topology DB[V45(ns3=50)] <- Heartbeat(Sender=V5(ns3=10), beacon_sending_time=5.000, sourced from old RSU report)  IMPERSONATING V5(ns3=10)
  Different claimed vs. slot identity -> impersonation evidence
  No external packet sent — attack is entirely internal to Ctrl0(ns3=0)

[t=7.000]  STEP ⑥  FAULTY ROUTING CONSEQUENCES
  Ctrl0(ns3=0) now holds conflicting liveness:
    V5(ns3=10) : beacon_sending_time=5.000 < current t=7.000  [STALE]
    V45(ns3=50) : beacon_sending_time=5.000 < current t=7.000  [STALE/FORGED — claims to be V5(ns3=10)]
  Two liveness entries now assert the same identity (V5(ns3=10)) under different slots
  Packets may be routed using stale/non-existent liveness
  Expected impact: packet loss, added delay, degraded PDR
  <- ATTACK SUCCESS (no external packet)
